---
title: "Checklist"
format: html
---

A Quarto Manual is an executable operations manual for a project. It does not
do the final scientific work for the user. It helps the user assemble,
configure, inspect, and verify the project so that the work can be done
deliberately and visibly.

One useful way to think about a manual is through aviation. A flight manual is
broader than a pre-flight checklist: it can cover preparation, operation,
inspection, and verification. In the same way, a Quarto Manual can guide setup
steps, operating procedures, and checks across the life of a project.

The checklist is one structural view of the manual:

- the full manual is the operations guide;
- the checklist is a summary of the manual's ordered pages;
- each page is one operational step or preparation stage;
- each page explains what must already be true;
- each page shows what to do next;
- each page proves whether that step worked.

The manual should move in order from page to page. Earlier pages establish
conditions that later pages rely on. By the time the user reaches the final
page, they should be able to answer questions like:

> Is this project ready to operate?
> Has this procedure been carried out correctly?
> What still needs to be done?

## Checklist Structure

A Quarto Manual checklist is derived from the manual's ordered pages. Each page
should have a
clear purpose and should leave behind evidence that the step was completed.
That evidence should usually come from the real project state: files,
directories, configuration, rendered outputs, logs, and passing checks.

Use the page metadata to declare where a page belongs in the checklist:

```yaml
---
title: "Assemble Python Environment"
manual:
  page: 2
---
```

The `manual.page` field gives the page its place in the manual. The checklist
view can then use that ordering to summarize the manual, report missing
sections, and help the user see how much of the procedure has been covered.

## What a Checklist Measures

A good checklist is not just a set of instructions. It also measures whether
the manual is structurally complete and whether each page can prove its own
outcome.

For example, a Quarto Manual can warn when:

- a page has no prerequisite block;
- a page has no check block;
- a page has no procedure block;
- pages are missing numbers or appear out of order.

It can also summarize useful manual-level facts, such as:

- the number of pages in the checklist;
- the number of checks across the manual;
- which pages are missing required sections.

## Authoring Guidance

When you write a Quarto Manual, focus on explicit procedure rather than hidden
automation.

Each page should help the user:

1. inspect the current project state;
2. understand one setup step;
3. perform that step in an editable, visible way;
4. verify that the step succeeded.

The checklist is complete when the manual has enough structure to guide the
user through the procedure and verify the result. The manual itself may be used
to prepare a project, operate it, inspect it, or hand it off.

---

## Implementation

One possible implementation is a `Checklist` `dataclass` that summarizes a
manual and its pages. In that design, the checklist is not the manual itself.
It is a structured representation of the manual's ordered steps. Each page has
a number, title, and semantic content for prerequisite, procedure, and check
blocks.


```{python}
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Sequence


CheckFn = Callable[["Checklist", "Page"], None]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Page:
    """One checklist step in a Quarto Manual."""

    title: str
    number: int
    prerequisite: str
    procedures: tuple[str, ...]
    check: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.title.strip():
            raise ValueError("Page.title must not be empty.")

        if self.number < 1:
            raise ValueError("Page.number must be >= 1.")

        if not self.prerequisite.strip():
            raise ValueError("Page.prerequisite must not be empty.")

        if not self.check.strip():
            raise ValueError("Page.check must not be empty.")

        if len(self.procedures) < 1:
            raise ValueError("Page.procedures must contain at least one procedure block.")

        if any(not step.strip() for step in self.procedures):
            raise ValueError("Page.procedures may not contain empty procedure blocks.")

    @property
    def procedure_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.procedures)

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "title": self.title,
            "number": self.number,
            "prerequisite": self.prerequisite,
            "procedure_count": self.procedure_count,
            "check": self.check,
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Checklist:
    """Declarative description of a Quarto Manual."""

    title: str
    project_root: Path
    pages: tuple[Page, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.title.strip():
            raise ValueError("Checklist.title must not be empty.")

        if len(self.pages) < 1:
            raise ValueError("Checklist.pages must contain at least one page.")

        numbers = [page.number for page in self.pages]
        if len(numbers) != len(set(numbers)):
            raise ValueError("Checklist page numbers must be unique.")

        if numbers != sorted(numbers):
            raise ValueError("Checklist pages must be ordered by page number.")

    @property
    def page_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.pages)

    @property
    def check_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.pages)

    @property
    def procedure_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(page.procedure_count for page in self.pages)

    def get_page(self, number: int) -> Page:
        for page in self.pages:
            if page.number == number:
                return page
        raise KeyError(f"No page found for number {number}.")

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "title": self.title,
            "project_root": str(self.project_root),
            "page_count": self.page_count,
            "procedure_count": self.procedure_count,
            "check_count": self.check_count,
            "pages": [page.summary() for page in self.pages],
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"Checklist("
            f"title={self.title!r}, "
            f"pages={self.page_count}, "
            f"project_root={str(self.project_root)!r})"
        )
```
